subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what security guarantee should it make across top-level navigations, redirects, subframes, subresources, downloads, and proxy-routed browser profiles?
rationale: The request adds operator-trusted security/config semantics beyond current SSRF hostname allowlists, so automation should not choose the permanent browser policy boundary or default list behavior.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped deny/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and tests against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Make the broader egress-firewall work own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser-specific redirects, proxy routing, and resource-loading behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable denylist and instead expose best-effort bot-blocked-site warnings that do not claim to provide an egress-control boundary.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the browser-scoped deny/warn semantics, then implement schema, guard, docs, and tests against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history across browser SSRF config, navigation policy, and security docs.
